name: Caelestiventus
sum: Large Late Triassic dimorphodontid from a desert-dune setting in Utah — the only known desert-dwelling non-pterodactyloid.
wsnote: At least 1.5 m, from an individual that was not fully grown.
holotype: BYU 20707 — Saints & Sinners Quarry, Nugget Sandstone, NE Utah.
material: Much of the skull (skull roof, face, complete mandible) and the last wing-finger bone.
exceptional: Uncrushed braincase allowed the first endocranial reconstruction of a Triassic pterosaur.
biology: Deep, narrow Dimorphodon-like skull; a possible throat pouch may have stored prey or served in display. Shows early pterosaurs were already ecologically diverse.
author: Britt et al. 2018

species.name: Caelestiventus hanseni
species.author: Britt et al. 2018
